specialty_roots.name: Small Fixes (Repair & Keep-Up)
specialty_roots.meaning: repairing, maintaining, and protecting parts of a home before small problems become expensive problems.
specialty_roots.customer_pain: minor defects, wear, leaks, failures, and neglected maintenance.
specialty_roots.desired_outcome: a home that works properly, stays protected, and avoids preventable damage.
specialty_roots.risk_objection: a small issue turning into a larger repair bill.
specialty_roots.buying_triggers: something stops working, starts leaking, looks worn, or is overdue for maintenance.
specialty_roots.trust_signals: clear diagnosis, before-and-after evidence, itemized scope, and workmanship assurance.

marketing_angles.name: Pain / Problem
marketing_angles.copy: Lead with the problem the customer already feels: minor defects, wear, leaks, failures, and neglected maintenance. Hook: “Dealing with minor defects, wear, leaks, failures, and neglected maintenance? Get a local quote for small fixes (repair & keep-up) before the problem becomes harder to ignore.” Position the service as the direct path to a home that works properly, stays protected, and avoids preventable damage. CTA: Request a quote.

marketing_angles.name: Prevention
marketing_angles.copy: Sell prevention, not just repair. Explain that timely small fixes (repair & keep-up) can help prevent a small issue turning into a larger repair bill. Hook: “A small warning sign today can become a much larger job later.” CTA: Get the issue checked and priced now.

marketing_angles.name: Cost of Delay
marketing_angles.copy: Frame inaction as a measurable business decision. Show the homeowner what waiting can expose them to: a small issue turning into a larger repair bill. Hook: “The cheapest time to deal with this is usually before the damage spreads.” CTA: Compare local quotes before delaying.

marketing_angles.name: Fast Relief / Speed
marketing_angles.copy: Emphasize response time and momentum. Use something stops working, starts leaking, looks worn, or is overdue for maintenance as the moment to act. Hook: “Need a solution without spending the next week calling contractors?” Promise fast matching, fast quoting, and a clear next step without promising unrealistic completion times.

marketing_angles.name: Trust & Professionalism
marketing_angles.copy: Reduce contractor anxiety. Center the message on clear diagnosis, before-and-after evidence, itemized scope, and workmanship assurance. Hook: “Know who is coming, what is being quoted, and what the job includes.” CTA: Compare professionals on scope, not just price.

marketing_angles.name: Local Expertise
marketing_angles.copy: Localize the message to weather, housing stock, bylaws, typical property types, and service availability in the neighbourhood. Hook: “Find small fixes (repair & keep-up) providers who actually serve your area.” CTA: Enter postal code and project details.

marketing_angles.name: Safety
marketing_angles.copy: Make the safety case concrete: poorly handled work can contribute to a small issue turning into a larger repair bill. Hook: “Some home jobs are expensive when done twice—and dangerous when done wrong.” CTA: Get a qualified professional quote.

marketing_angles.name: Property Value
marketing_angles.copy: Connect the project to protecting or improving the property. Explain how a home that works properly, stays protected, and avoids preventable damage can support maintenance, buyer confidence, usability, or curb appeal. Hook: “Protect the house you already paid for.” CTA: Price the upgrade.

marketing_angles.name: Comfort / Quality of Life
marketing_angles.copy: Sell the day-to-day benefit, not the technical work. Translate repairing, maintaining, and protecting parts of a home before small problems become expensive problems into a better living experience: a home that works properly, stays protected, and avoids preventable damage. Hook: “The real product is a home that works better every day.” CTA: Tell us what you want improved.

marketing_angles.name: Convenience / Done-for-You
marketing_angles.copy: Target customers who value time. Hook: “Describe the job once instead of calling company after company.” Position Quotes.pro as the intake layer that turns one project description into comparable contractor conversations.

marketing_angles.name: Family / Household Protection
marketing_angles.copy: Frame the service around protecting the people using the home. Tie the message to avoiding a small issue turning into a larger repair bill and achieving a home that works properly, stays protected, and avoids preventable damage. Hook: “Fix the house problem before it becomes a household problem.” CTA: Request local help.

marketing_angles.name: Efficiency / Operating Cost
marketing_angles.copy: Highlight operating efficiency where relevant: wasted water, electricity, heating, cooling, maintenance time, or repeated service calls. Hook: “A proper fix can cost less than living with an inefficient problem month after month.” CTA: Compare repair and upgrade options.

marketing_angles.name: Seasonal / Timing
marketing_angles.copy: Create seasonal campaigns around the most natural trigger: something stops working, starts leaking, looks worn, or is overdue for maintenance. Hook: “Do it before the busy season, not during it.” Adapt the copy by climate and month for each Canadian region.

marketing_angles.name: Guarantee / Risk Reversal
marketing_angles.copy: Use risk reversal carefully: promote written scopes, workmanship terms, warranties where offered, and documented expectations. Hook: “No vague handshake job—get the scope in writing.” Never claim a guarantee unless the contractor actually provides it.

marketing_angles.name: Before-and-After Transformation
marketing_angles.copy: Use visual transformation. Show the 'before' state implied by minor defects, wear, leaks, failures, and neglected maintenance, then the 'after' state: a home that works properly, stays protected, and avoids preventable damage. Hook: “From problem area to finished result.” Best channels: short video, carousel, photo ad, landing-page slider.

marketing_angles.name: Transparent Quote
marketing_angles.copy: Make pricing transparency the offer. Hook: “Know what is included before you say yes.” Encourage itemized or clearly scoped quotes, site-visit requirements where needed, exclusions, material assumptions, and estimated timelines.

marketing_angles.name: DIY vs Professional
marketing_angles.copy: Contrast DIY effort with professional execution without insulting the homeowner. Hook: “You can spend the weekend troubleshooting—or get a professional to diagnose and quote it properly.” Mention specialized tools, code, safety, access, or finish quality when relevant.

marketing_angles.name: Landlord / Property Manager
marketing_angles.copy: Create a B2B version for landlords, property managers, real-estate teams, and small portfolios. Hook: “One property issue is a repair; ten properties need a system.” Emphasize repeat service, documentation, scheduling, and quote consistency.

marketing_angles.name: New Homeowner / Move-In
marketing_angles.copy: Target new owners and movers. Hook: “Just got the keys? Fix the unknowns before they become your first surprise bill.” Tie small fixes (repair & keep-up) to inspection follow-ups, move-in upgrades, and making the property fit the owner.

marketing_angles.name: Preparedness / Future-Proofing
marketing_angles.copy: Position the service as future-proofing. Hook: “Fix today’s issue in a way that makes the next upgrade easier.” Connect the project to future renovations, capacity, maintenance access, resale, resilience, or changing household needs.

marketing_angles.name: Budget / Financing / Phasing
marketing_angles.copy: Address price sensitivity directly. Hook: “Get the right scope first, then decide what to do now and what can wait.” Encourage alternate materials, phased work, repair-vs-replace comparisons, and financing only where a real provider offers it.

marketing_angles.name: Social Proof / Reputation
marketing_angles.copy: Use reputation as proof: verified reviews, project photos, local references, years in trade, repeat customers, and response history. Hook: “See evidence before you invite someone into your home.” Never fabricate ratings, testimonials, or project counts.

marketing_angles.name: DIY vs Professional
marketing_angles.copy: Contrast DIY effort with professional execution without insulting the homeowner. Hook: “You can spend the weekend troubleshooting—or get a professional to diagnose and quote it properly.” Mention specialized tools, code, safety, access, or finish quality when relevant.

marketing_angles.name: Landlord / Property Manager
marketing_angles.copy: Create a B2B version for landlords, property managers, real-estate teams, and small portfolios. Hook: “One property issue is a repair; ten properties need a system.” Emphasize repeat service, documentation, scheduling, and quote consistency.

marketing_angles.name: New Homeowner / Move-In
marketing_angles.copy: Target new owners and movers. Hook: “Just got the keys? Fix the unknowns before they become your first surprise bill.” Tie picking paint colors and furniture layouts to inspection follow-ups, move-in upgrades, and making the property fit the owner.

marketing_angles.name: Preparedness / Future-Proofing
marketing_angles.copy: Position the service as future-proofing. Hook: “Fix today’s issue in a way that makes the next upgrade easier.” Connect the project to future renovations, capacity, maintenance access, resale, resilience, or changing household needs.

marketing_angles.name: Budget / Financing / Phasing
marketing_angles.copy: Address price sensitivity directly. Hook: “Get the right scope first, then decide what to do now and what can wait.” Encourage alternate materials, phased work, repair-vs-replace comparisons, and financing only where a real provider offers it.

marketing_angles.name: Social Proof / Reputation
marketing_angles.copy: Use reputation as proof: verified reviews, project photos, local references, years in trade, repeat customers, and response history. Hook: “See evidence before you invite someone into your home.” Never fabricate ratings, testimonials, or project counts.
